summary: The basic Angular upgrade flows pass, but the implementation does not provide the required atomic concurrency guarantee and directs `add` to a different directory than the metadata when a custom Angular UI path is configured.

findings.summary: Concurrent add/upgrade operations silently lose component snapshot metadata; implement a project-scoped lock or atomic read-modify-write protocol and add concurrent regression coverage.
findings.evidence: Two concurrent `company-angular add` calls for button and input both return success, but the resulting company-components.json retains only button while index.ts exports both. This violates the planned no-lost-metadata/no-interleaved-writes contract.

findings.summary: Make Angular add use the resolved UI path from company-components.json or --ui-dir consistently for validation, writes, barrel generation, and metadata.
findings.evidence: After `init --ui-dir src/custom-ui`, `add button` writes src/app/ui/button.ts but records src/custom-ui in metadata. A later upgrade follows metadata and reports the component missing.
